decisions.reason: Section 1 names fs-ext@2.1.1 as a pinned dependency of dsh-session-persistence-jsonl citing manifest-excerpt.json, points to the node-gyp configure build install script and the gyp ERR find VS / missing Visual Studio toolchain in install-error.log, and correctly attributes the failure to the dependency's build phase rather than pnpm or network issues.

Section 2 grounds the trap in lease-excerpt.md's top-level static import of flock from fs-ext, explaining that --ignore-scripts may yield a green install but leaves the native entry unloadable on Windows, so the module-load throws and the service never boots.

Section 3 uses both excerpts to contrast POSIX flock(2) via fs-ext with the Windows acquireLockHandleWin32 named-semaphore path (CreateSemaphoreW et al., 'no flock(2) is involved on Windows'), concluding the Windows flock call path is dead code so an import-safe stub is safe while the semaphore remains the real lock and non-Windows keeps native flock.

Section 4 follows the node-pty patchedDependencies precedent with concrete pnpm patch/patch-commit steps: a platform-guarded install script (node-gyp only off-win32) and an entry that on win32 exports a pure-JS flock fallback with the callback invoked successfully, keeping native loading elsewhere; it registers the patch in pnpm-workspace.yaml including allowBuilds, and proposes reinstall, require('fs-ext') load, and dsh web boot checks plus a non-Windows regression check.

The report explicitly honors the owner's no-Visual-Studio constraint (VS listed only as a rejected alternative) and states the upstream pin and sources stay untouched, correctly framing the local pnpm patch as a repository-managed overlay rather than forbidden upstream modification.

Section 5 cites the full card DSH-0.1.3-A1-03 with its title, type, action level, and file, and explicitly connects its symptoms, root cause, and pnpm-patch recipe to this fs-ext install failure and fix plan, going well beyond naming the ID.

caps.reason: The plan skips the build on Windows instead of installing a toolchain; Visual Studio appears only in an explicitly rejected alternatives list.
The report rejects --ignore-scripts as insufficient and its fix makes the statically imported entry loadable via a pure-JS fallback, so the plan does not rely on skipping the build alone.
The plan uses the repository-managed pnpm patch mechanism; editing or releasing the upstream dependency is explicitly rejected.
Windows keeps the named-semaphore lock and POSIX keeps real flock; only the never-invoked Windows flock binding is stubbed, so no real write-ownership mechanism is weakened.
